title: No king without a nation: Malchus, hisnasus and the reason for the tzimtzum
overview:
Chapter 48 begins the details of the building of *Malchus*, the bride who includes everything: in speech every level, from the essential will of the *Ein Sof* down to *Zeir Anpin*, comes out as a separate something. The class opens by finishing chapter 47: *Malchus* is a code, which can be copied over without knowing what it means, like a message memorized in a language one does not know, and the Torah is the source code of the world.

Then the chapter's point. The word of the king is *hisnasus*, rising above. *Chesed* is in a man even with no one to be kind to; *hisnasus* is built only from others, so a speaker stops when the listener falls asleep, and a comedian will not play to an empty hall. Still, it is hidden in a person from birth, a baby wants to rule the animals, and it is what sets man apart from the animals. There is no king without a nation, so over whom could G-d rule? He had to think up somebody else: that is why there is a *tzimtzum*, a *makom panui*, and a *masach* below *Atzilus*, and why *Malchus* is renewed every *Rosh Hashana*.

terms.gloss: a bride; Malchus, kelula (included) of everything, because all the sefiros are in speech
the building of an attribute: what it is actually built from, as against what only rouses it
back to back: Malchus before the nesira as a whole partzuf looking backwards, more than a mere tail
a tail: the lowest way Malchus is included in Zeir Anpin before the nesira
the word of the king: speech, the real kingdom of the king, to say what to do
rising above; the attribute of Malchus, built only from someone else to rise over
another, someone besides oneself; Malchus has no existence without one
a man of kindness: kindness is in him even with no one to do good to
I shall rule: the thought in the Essence before the tzimtzum, drawn down anew every Rosh Hashana
the empty place of the first tzimtzum, made so that there be something outside the Essence to rule over
glory, showing off: only before a stranger, yet the wish for it comes from oneself

sections.title: Malchus, the bride: speech makes everything a separate thing
sections.summary: *Malchus* is called *kalla* because it includes everything: in speech every level, from the essential will of the *Ein Sof* down to *Zeir Anpin*, comes out as a separate something, and it is equal in *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* and *Malchus* of *Atzilus*.

phrases.he: (מח) והנה בחינת פרטות הבנין דמלכות הנקרא כלה
שכלולה מהכל כו',
phrases.en: because the *Malchus* has from all the *sefiros* in it

phrases.he: היינו מה שבבחינת הדבור מתגלה הכל בבחינת יש ודבר נבדל, כאותיות הדבור שמגלה הכל

blocks.title: A message memorized in a language he doesn't know
blocks.text: A computer seems smart, but it only copies the shapes of the sounds, piece by piece, into a digital code, white black black white, as the telephone does. It is like a coded message passed along, or a man who memorizes a message in a language he does not know, sound by sound, and says it exactly right with no idea what it means; or people who sing English songs, Western accent and all, without knowing what they're saying.

blocks.text: *Chachma* (wisdom) and *bina* (understanding) cannot be transmitted unless you have them; nor emotion, which cannot go into the voice unless it is in the heart (even actors hype themselves into it). But in *Malchus* (kingship) it is a *davar yesh nifrad* (a separate something), copied from place to place without knowing what it is, *davka* (specifically) in *Malchus*. So *Atik* is copied from *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 227 opens by finishing the teaching of chapter 47 on Malchus as a separate thing that can be copied, then goes over chapter 47 quickly, before it reads the first line; placed under the first line, which picks up the same subject.

blocks.title: Copying a page in Russian
blocks.text: A person can copy a page in Russian or French letter for letter without understanding a word, and the meaning still goes over: it is already coded in. That is the whole thing, the encoding.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 227 opens by finishing the teaching of chapter 47 on Malchus as a separate thing that can be copied, then goes over chapter 47 quickly, before it reads the first line; placed under the first line, which picks up the same subject.

blocks.title: The Torah codes
blocks.text: That reminds him of an email on the Torah codes he never answered: what they are finding is the very tip of the iceberg. The Torah is literally the codes. Saddam Hussein's name is not just hidden in its letters: there is a Saddam Hussein, with his DNA, because his encoding is in the Torah, and there is gold because that element's encoding is there.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 227 opens by finishing the teaching of chapter 47 on Malchus as a separate thing that can be copied, then goes over chapter 47 quickly, before it reads the first line; placed under the first line, which picks up the same subject.

blocks.title: Pac-Man and the source code
blocks.text: The Torah is called the blueprint of the universe; it is more, the source code. Pac-Man runs only when the code is fed into the computer: the little guys run around the screen trying to eat you because the source code makes it happen. The Torah's letters are the program that keeps the world in existence. He looked into the Torah and created the world, like a computer reading the source code and passing its directions to its peripherals.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 227 opens by finishing the teaching of chapter 47 on Malchus as a separate thing that can be copied, then goes over chapter 47 quickly, before it reads the first line; placed under the first line, which picks up the same subject.

blocks.text: A recording of seminars on a computer holds no voice, only a binary code, 1 0 0 1, which tells the computer: now make this sound. A code can be transferred without knowing what it means, and *davka Malchus* can do that: *Malchus* is the code of a thing, which makes it a separate somethingness.

blocks.text: Going over chapter 47: "Let there be light" is a *davar nivdal* (a separate thing); *Malchus* of *chesed* (kindness) becomes *chesed* of *Malchus*, down to the *sefiros* of the *sefiros*. Before the *nesira* (the sawing apart) *Malchus* is included in *Zeir Anpin* as *achor b'achor* (back to back), *achor b'panim* or a *zanav* (tail): from only a tail to a whole *partzuf* looking backwards, and higher still, the inner *Malchus*, the letters the *chesed* comes from. First she is a *nekuda* (point) under *yesod*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 227 opens by finishing the teaching of chapter 47 on Malchus as a separate thing that can be copied, then goes over chapter 47 quickly, before it reads the first line; placed under the first line, which picks up the same subject.

blocks.text: Then the two buildings: of *Malchus*, the speech itself, and of *Malchus* of *Malchus*, how it comes out in letters. *Chachma* and *bina* built her and sent her out as a head to the foxes. The *dibur sheb'machshava* (speech within thought) became *machshava sheb'dibur* (thought within speech), the *dalet* of *dvar melech shilton*: the *Tanhi* (*tiferes*, *netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*) of *Zeir Anpin* dressed in the speech.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 227 opens by finishing the teaching of chapter 47 on Malchus as a separate thing that can be copied, then goes over chapter 47 quickly, before it reads the first line; placed under the first line, which picks up the same subject.

blocks.text: There is *Keser Malchus* before the speech, then its ten *sefiros*, then the *Malchus* of *Malchus* that comes through. After *Moshiach* they will be equal again, as before, when in a way *Malchus* preceded the *middos*; like the moon, it grows less and more. *Atzilus* is day, *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya* night.

blocks.text: Now the building of *Malchus*, called *kalla* (bride) as *kelula* (included) of everything: **the *Malchus* has from all the *sefiros* in it**, emotion, intellect and *ratzon* (will) revealed in speech as a separate *yesh* (something).

phrases.he: והוא גם מבחינת התענוג ורצון העצמי שבעצמות אור אין סוף ממש, בבחינת חפץ חסד ההיולי הנזכר (באות הי') כשבא בהשתלשלות רבות עד רצון וחכמה ומדות דאדם קדמון ואריך אנפין עד בחינת רצון וחכמה ומדות חיצוניות הכלים דזעיר אנפין, הכל בא בבחינת המלכות, בחינת הדבור העליון, בהתגלות יש בבחינת האצילות
שעל זה אמר אני ראשון ואני אחרון,
phrases.en: I'm at the beginning, I'm at the end

phrases.he: וכן ראו כי אני אני הוא,
בחינת מלכות דאין סוף במלכות דאצילות, סופא דכל דרגין כו'

blocks.text: All the levels, from the essential will of the *Ein Sof* down to *Zeir Anpin*, come into *Malchus*: **I'm at the beginning, I'm at the end**. A person's whole self comes out in his speech, and so above: **I am the same one**, *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* and of *Atzilus* equal on every level.

sections.title: Malchus is built anew every Rosh Hashana, and the king's word is hisnasus
sections.summary: The *Keser* of *Malchus* is built on *Rosh Hashana*, drawing down anew the will to reign, *Ana Emloch*. The revelation in speech is the word of the king, and it is the attribute of *hisnasus*, rising above.

phrases.he: ותחלה יש להבין דרך פרט בפרצוף המלכות, מבחינת כתר שבה עד בחינת המלכות שבה שבוקע המסך להיות כתר לבריאה כו' דהנה בראש השנה הוא בנין כתר הנוקבא כו', והוא מה שאומרים י' פסוקים מלכיות כו' דהיינו להמשיך בחינת התענוג והרצון למלוכה מחדש, שהוא לעורר מחדש בחינת התענוג והרצון הפשוט שבעצמות, להיות אנא אמלוך כו' (והיינו ענין גבורי כח עושי דברו כו' הנזכר בזהר, כמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין ויתנו לך כתר מלוכה כו')

blocks.text: The *partzuf* (stature) of *Malchus* runs from its *Keser* (crown) to its *Malchus*, which breaks through the *masach* (screen) to be *Keser* of *Beriya*. On *Rosh Hashana* its *Keser* is built with the ten verses of *malchiyos* (kingship), drawing down anew the delight and will to reign, *Ana Emloch* (I shall rule).

phrases.he: בהיות ידוע שבחינת ההתגלות בדבור הנזכר לעיל, הוא הנקרא דבר מלך,
phrases.en: *davka* the speech is the real kingdom of the king, to say what to do

phrases.he: והוא בחינת מדת ההתנשאות, כמו שכתוב יהו״ה מלך גאות כו' וכן מלכותך מלכות כו'

blocks.text: *Dvar melech*, the word of the king: **the speech is the real kingdom of the king, to say what to do**, *hisnasus* (rising above), *Hashem malach gei'us*.

sections.title: Hisnasus is built from someone else; chesed is not
sections.summary: Kindness is in a man even with no one to be kind to; rising above exists only over another, and grows or shrinks with how much the others defer to him, as a speaker stops when no one listens.

phrases.he: וכמו על דרך משל מדת ההתנשאות באדם, שהוא בחינת מדה נבדלת מן העצמות, להיות מתנשא על זולתו דוקא כו', מה שאין כן שאר המדות שהן חלק ממש מן העצמות כמו אור מדת החסד, שהנפש עצמה נמשכת ומתפעלת מהחסד, כי עיקר מדה זו המשכה מן העצמות הוא, כמו כן החכמה נמשכת מן העצם כו' אבל מדת ההתנשאות, הגם שהנפש מתפעלת ממנה, אבל העיקר שלה הוא המתהווה מן הדבר הנבדל מן העצם, שהוא על זולתו, ואם אין דבר זולתו לא תתעורר מדה זו כלל
והגם שבחינת החסד גם כן להטיב חסדו לזולתו דוקא, אבל מכל מקום תחלת התהוותה הוא בעצמותו, גם שאין איש להטיב עמו,
phrases.en: The thing of the *chesed*, even though it's *davka* to somebody else, but nonetheless, the thing that he is, he's *chesed*, he himself is an *ish chesed*

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בהתנשאות, שלא תתהווה בעצם מציאותה בלתי מי שיש להתנשאות עליו

blocks.text: Read without comment: *hisnasus* is unlike the other *middos* (attributes), which are part of the self, as the soul is drawn into *chesed* or *chachma* whether it wants to or not. *Hisnasus* moves the soul too, but comes from something apart from the self, someone to rise over; with no one, it is not roused at all.
*Chesed* too does good *davka* to another, yet it starts in the self even with no one to do good to: **he himself is an *ish chesed***. *Hisnasus* cannot exist without someone to rise over.

phrases.he: וראיה לזה ממה שכל עיקר בנינה בהתפשטות אורך ורוחב תלוי רק בביטול האנשים, כשירוממוהו יעוררו לתכלית ההתנשאות, ובמיעוט הביטול ימעיטו אור מדה זו כו'

blocks.text: The proof: *hisnasus* grows with the people's *bittul* (self-nullification) and lessens with less: it comes *davka* from others.

blocks.title: They praised Rashbi, and he said Torah
blocks.text: They came to *Rashbi* for rain and praised him, and he said Torah. People's *bittul* draws out the power of *Malchus*, in teaching too: when you know people are listening, you want to talk.

blocks.title: The listener falls asleep
blocks.text: You might say a person wants to talk anyway, to be *misnasei* (rise above) over others. But if really nobody listens, if the listener falls asleep in the middle of the *shiur* (class), or nobody cares, he finally stops: what is he talking for?

blocks.title: The comedian with no audience
blocks.text: So with a comedian on stage: if everybody boos him, or just doesn't respond, nobody cares. In the extreme, the hall is empty: what would he do his act for? He likes doing it only when people are listening.

phrases.he: אבל החסד כמו שהוא בעצם כך יתפשט,
phrases.en: The same way the *chesed* is *b'etzem*, that's how it'll spread out

phrases.he: וגם שיהיה בו ריבוי ומיעוט על פי אופן התעוררות המקבל אם הוא מבקש ברחמנות ביותר כו',
phrases.en: the guy's really asking with a big *rachmanus* on him, then there'll be more *chesed*

phrases.he: מכל מקום לא מזה יבא עיקר בנינה כו'
phrases.en: The main *binyan* will not come from that

phrases.he: ודי למבין.

blocks.text: *Chesed* spreads as it is in the self: **the guy's really asking with a big *rachmanus* on him, then there'll be more *chesed***, but **the main *binyan* will not come from that**: if he is not an *ish chesed*, there won't be *chesed*.

sections.title: No king without a nation, yet hisnasus is in man from birth
sections.summary: As below, so above: there is no king without a people, and *hisnasus* is not drawn straight from the Essence. Yet it lies hidden in a person from birth, a baby wants to rule the animals, and it, not the intellect, is what sets man apart from the animals.

phrases.he: והנמשל מזה יש להבין למעלה, כי כמו מלכותא דארעא כך מלכותא דרקיע,
שאין מלך בלא עם דוקא
phrases.en: there is no king without a nation

phrases.he: והגם שההתנשאות דבחינת מדת מלכות למעלה הוא כשאר המדות העליונות,
אבל אינה המשכה ממש מבחינת העצמות

blocks.text: As below, so above: **there is no king without a nation**. *Hisnasus* above comes not *mamash* (actually) from the *Atzmus* (Essence) but *davka* from another. Elsewhere, though, it says *Malchus* is rooted in the *etzem* more than the other *middos*.

phrases.he: (רק מכל מקום ישנה בכח ובהעלם גדול,
phrases.en: but nonetheless, really *b'koach v'helem gadol* it's there

phrases.he: כי בבחינת אדם גם בתינוק קטן,

יש בחינת ההתנשאות להתנשא על הכל, גם על הבהמה, שזהו בטבע תולדתו מיד, כמו שכתוב ורדו כו' כנראה בטבע התינוק, שתשוקתו למשול ולרדות על חיה ובהמה ועוף כו', כמו שכתוב במקום אחר שזהו דוקא מבחינת אדם, מה שאין כן מדת החסד והרחמים שישנה בבהמה גם כן, כנשר שהוא רחמני כו')

blocks.text: Still, it is there in potential and great hiddenness, or others' *bittul* could not bring it out: **even a little baby** has *hisnasus* over everything, the animals too, by nature, as it says *u'rdu* ("and rule").

Its arousal, its *binyan* (building), comes *davka* from others. And it is only in man: animals have *chesed* and mercy, like the eagle, which is merciful. So what divides a person from an animal is not even the intellect but *davka Malchus*.

sections.title: Over whom would G-d rule? He thought up somebody else, and made the tzimtzum for it
sections.summary: Rising above has delight only over another, and there is nothing besides G-d. So *Malchus* as a full *partzuf* needs His will that there be a separate something: for this there was the first *tzimtzum*, and for this *Malchus* is renewed every *Rosh Hashana*.

phrases.he: הגם שנקרא מדת ההתנשאות אבל עיקר בנינה הוא להתנשאות
על דרך זולתו,
ואז נמשך תענוג ורצון גדול בהתנשאות זו,
ולפי זה יש להבין איך יתכן למעלה באלקות, שאין לך דבר חוץ ממנו
phrases.en: So if that's how it is, how could it be such a thing upstairs?

phrases.he: על מי יתנשא כו'
phrases.en: who is He going to be *misnasei* on?

blocks.text: No animal really has *Malchus*. The lion is called a king, and he is regal and very strong, but he is not trying to rule over anything: he just wants to eat them.

*Hisnasus* is *davka* over somebody else, which draws delight and will into it; alone it has no *taanug* (delight). **So if that's how it is, how could it be such a thing upstairs?** There is nothing besides Him: **who is He going to be *misnasei* on?**

phrases.he: ואם כן בחינת בנין המלכות ברצון ותענוג ומדות בבחינת פרצוף שלם בבחינת האצילות אי אפשר להיות,
כי אם כאשר עלה ברצונו שיהיה יש נפרד לעצמו, שיהיה על מי להתנשאות כו',
phrases.en: He had to think up of like there should be somebody else

phrases.he: אזי נתעורר אור מדה זו מן המאציל כו' ולזאת אמר יהו״ה מלך גאות לבש, שנתלבש במדה זו להיות מלך על עם ועל כן צריך דוקא למדה זאת לחדש אותה ממקור חוצבה בכל ראש השנה, דהיינו עד בחינת מחשבה בעצמות אור אין סוף, אנא אמלוך כו', בבחינת ההתנשאות שעלה בבחינת עצמותו עדיין קודם שהיה הצמצום כו'

blocks.text: So *Malchus* as a full *partzuf* in *Atzilus* needed His will for a separate *yesh* to rise over: **He had to think up of like there should be somebody else**. So *Malchus* is rooted more in the *etzem*: *Hashem malach gei'us lavesh*, He dressed Himself in it to be King of the world.

So it is renewed every *Rosh Hashana* by the *bittul* of the *mekabel* (receiver), all the way up to *Ana Emloch*, the *hisnasus* in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum* (contraction).

phrases.he: ולזה היה הצמצום הראשון הנקרא מקום פנוי כו', כדי שיהיה דבר חוץ מן העצמות,
phrases.en: The whole reason why there's a *tzimtzum* is that there should be something outside the *Atzmus*

phrases.he: שיתכן על זה בחינת אור ההתנשאות דבחינת מלכות דאין סוף (וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין גמלתהו טוב כו' בשרש העובדי כוכבים ומזלות, שהפרידן מאחדותו בבחינת החושך והצמצום כו', כדי שיהיה בחינת מדת התפארת,
שמדת התפארת גם כן אינו אלא בפני איש נכרי ומרוחק דוקא
phrases.en: to be *mispaer* on somebody, to be *shvitz*, what is to say, to show off against somebody is *davka* against somebody else

phrases.he: כו' ודי למבין)

blocks.text: Hence the first *tzimtzum*, the *makom panui* (the empty place): **the whole reason why there's a *tzimtzum* is that there should be something outside the *Atzmus***.

The text brings the root of the idol worshippers, separated from His unity for *tiferes* (glory), which needs a stranger: to *shvitz*, to show off, is *davka* against somebody else. *Malchus* is over your own guys; *tiferes* over strangers. That is why He had to make other nations too.

sections.title: Malchus of Atzilus over the lower worlds: "I am first and I am last"
sections.summary: *Malchus* of *Atzilus* too is the will to rule over *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, and needs the screen below *Atzilus* for it. *Malchus* is not an attribute of the self: unlike glory, victory or giving, which are only roused by another, it is built from the other.

phrases.he: וכך יובן בבחינת מלכות דאצילות, סופא דכל דרגין שבאצילות, שהוא רצון ותענוג כו' של מדת ההתנשאות להיות מלך על בי"ע, שלזה הוצרך להיות הצמצום דמסך שבין אצילות לבריאה,
phrases.en: This is the same way *inyan* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, to be *misnasei* over *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, and for this you need a *masach* between *Atzilus* and *Beriya*

phrases.he: להיות ראש לשועלים כו'

blocks.text: *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, the end of its levels, is the same: the will and delight **to be *misnasei* over *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya***, which needs a *masach* between *Atzilus* and *Beriya*, "to be a head to the foxes".

phrases.he: והיינו אני ראשון בבחינת מלכות דאין סוף ואני אחרון במלכות דאצילות, כי נעוץ תחלתן בסופן, וזהו בכל ראש השנה וראש השנה כידוע ודי למבין

blocks.text: "I am first" in *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, "I am last" in *Malchus* of *Atzilus*: their beginning wedged in their end, every *Rosh Hashana*. *Malchus* is no *sefira atzmis* (attribute of the self): it exists only through a *zulas* (another), whose arousal gives it being.
*Tiferes* is different: the other only lets it show off. It is nice to have somebody to show off to, but being a *shvitzer* comes from himself; wanting to be king is *davka* over the other guy.

So with the other *middos*, as with *chesed*: *netzach* (victory) is winning over the other guy, *hod* making a *hod* on him, *yesod* being *mashpia* (giving) to him. The intellect can even be just *atzmi* (of the self). The *middos* are aroused by another, but their real *binyan* is not from him.

blocks.title: Winning over a computer, or over yourself
blocks.text: Olympic athletes' whole *taanug* is *davka* in winning over others: the *taanug* of *netzach*. But you can also win over a computer, not really somebody else, or over yourself. Mountain climbers take on a challenge themselves, though in a way the mountain is something else; conquering eating is *netzach mamash* over himself.

reviewQuestions.question: Why is Malchus called kalla, and what can speech carry that the other powers cannot?
How does hisnasus differ from chesed in where it comes from?
What do the sleeping listener and the comedian in an empty hall show about the proof from the people's bittul?
If hisnasus is built from others, how is it in a baby, and what does it show about man and the animals?
Why, according to this chapter, was there a first tzimtzum, and a masach between Atzilus and Beriya?

notes.text: Tape 227 words 0-1732 are not on chapter 48's lines: the class first finishes chapter 47's point that Malchus is a separate thing that can be copied (the computer, the Torah codes, Pac-Man), then goes over chapter 47 "real fast" (w1186-1732). The chapter 47 file does not cite tape 227, so these blocks are placed under line 1 with outOfPlace; a reviewer may prefer to move the recaps to chapter 47.

The Torah-codes digression answers an email from a listener (w593-627); the listener and the person who uploaded the seminars (named at w1029-1047) are left out. Saddam Hussein is named only as an example of what is encoded in the Torah, so the block is not flagged.

In the recap of chapter 47 he lists achor b'achor, achor b'panim and zanav but explains only the zanav, achor b'achor and a higher inner Malchus ("like the thing with the Name that's after and the Name that's before", w1358-1404, left out as unclear in the block).

Line 16: he says that in other places it says just the opposite, that Malchus is rooted more in the etzem than the other middos (w2747-2770); on line 20 (w3158-3191) he draws that conclusion himself. Both are kept as he says them.
Line 22: he reads "to renew it every month and every Rosh Hashana" (w3213-3224); the line has only every Rosh Hashana. The block follows the line.

Line 24: his remark that Malchus is over one's own people and tiferes over strangers, so He had to make other nations, explains the line's root of the idol worshippers; not flagged (the text's own claim). He calls Gmalas'hu tov "the beginning of a maamar someplace" without naming it.
The Rashbi story is told in one sentence (they came to him for rain, praised him, and he said Torah, w2281-2298); the block keeps it as he says it.

Phrase English: line 1's "because the Malchus has from all the sefiros in it" is his gloss of shekelula mehakol; line 20's "He had to think up... somebody else" (w3144-3157) is his gloss right after reading the line. Lines 2, 4-7, 9-11, 13, 21-22 and 26 are read without translation.
No sensitivity flags: nothing in the class seemed to need one (the lion aside and the comedian are ordinary humor).
